title: Session hydration & token checkpointing to recover mid-generation tool calls for flaky clients
creator: Alex Kim
description:
Problem: Clients with intermittent connectivity regularly disconnect during long-running streaming generations. When those generations include function/tool invocations and structured outputs, we currently either: 1) hold GPU resources for long time windows waiting for clients to reconnect, or 2) garbage-collect partial generations and lose tool side-effects. Both outcomes increase cost, reduce reliability, and surface inconsistent application state to customers.

Goal: Introduce a lightweight session hydration & token checkpointing mechanism that: 1) allows safe resume semantics for clients that reconnect within a configurable staleness window, 2) marks in-progress generations with compact checkpoints so the runtime can free hot resources earlier, and 3) enforces atomicity hints around tool/function calls so external side-effects are either retriable or isolated.

Key ideas: 1) Checkpoint tokens: persist compact checkpoints (sequence id + KV-cache snapshot hash + resume_hint) at configurable intervals (e.g., every 128 tokens) to durable storage. Checkpoints are small opaque blobs returned to the client as resume_token. 2) Soft expiry / hydration window: maintain a configurable soft-expiry (default 90s) during which checkpoints are available for resume. After soft-expiry, runtime will attempt graceful finalization (flush prefixes to short-term cache) and mark the generation for archival. 3) Tool-call fencing: Before issuing a tool/function call that has external side-effects (webhook, DB write), emit a pre-call checkpoint and mark the call as "tentative". On reconnect, client can query checkpoint metadata to decide whether to re-run the tool or skip based on idempotency hints. 4) Resume API: add POST /v1/resume with resume_token and resume_strategy params (continue | restart-from-checkpoint). Response includes explicit structured output envelope indicating any tool invocations that completed server-side. 5) Compatibility layer: Clients that do not opt into resume semantics continue to observe current GC behavior; enhanced clients get better availability without changing existing API surface for simple calls.

Trade-offs considered: 1) Durability vs cost: storing full KV cache per checkpoint is expensive. We will store a compressed hash + delta-only checkpointing and fetch full cache on demand for long resumes. 2) Latency impact: periodic checkpointing can add a few ms per checkpoint. We will make checkpoint frequency configurable and default to coarse intervals for low-latency workloads. 3) Security: resume tokens are bearer-like; we will bind tokens to session id, model version, and require same API key or mutually authenticated client to use. 4) Tool semantics complexity: we must push idempotency responsibilities where feasible to tool integrations; runtime will provide structured metadata to help integrations decide whether to reapply effects.

Metrics / Signals to monitor:
- resume_attempt_rate, resume_success_rate, resume_latency_ms
- abandoned_generation_count, average_time_to_checkpoint_gc
- tool-invocation-duplicate-rate (proxy for incorrect idempotency handling)

SLOs and initial limits:
- Resume success target >= 98% for reconnections within soft-expiry window
- Checkpoint write latency p95 < 30ms
- Default soft-expiry = 90s, configurable per project

Acceptance criteria:
- New resume API endpoint implemented with end-to-end tests for continue/restart strategies
- Checkpoint persistence implemented with configurable retention and per-project quotas
- Tool call fencing hooks added to runtime and example integrations updated with idempotency hints
- Docs and SDK examples demonstrating resume flow and security considerations
- Load test showing <5% added tail latency at default checkpoint frequency (128 tokens)

Rollout plan: start alpha behind feature flag for a small set of internal customers and Redwood's sample-apps; monitor resume_failure and tool-duplicate metrics. Iterate on checkpoint frequency defaults and retention policy. Expand to public beta once metrics stable for 2 weeks.

Backward compatibility notes: The existing streaming APIs remain unchanged. Resume is opt-in: clients need to request checkpointing by sending header X-Checkpoint: enabled or by calling the SDK helper that sets the flag. If a client never enables checkpointing, runtime will follow existing GC path.

Longer-term considerations: explore lightweight client-side checkpoint caching to avoid round-trips on resume, and consider server-side shardable checkpoint stores to reduce read amplification for large KV caches.

acceptance_criteria: Checkpoint write path with configurable interval and retention
Tool-call fencing hooks + example idempotent integration in samples repo
E2E tests covering reconnect and resume success cases
Load test demonstrating acceptable latency impact
testing_steps: Unit tests for checkpoint blob encode/decode and access control binding
Integration test: simulate client disconnect at various token offsets and verify resume continues generation and restores KV-cache semantics
Chaos test: intermittent network with multiple reconnects and validate no duplicated tool side-effects beyond acceptable threshold
Beta customers: enable for 3 internal customers, collect metrics for 2 weeks
